label: STOPP L1: strong opioid as first line for mild pain
title: Strong opioid first for mild pain
statement: Use of oral or transdermal strong opioids (morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl, buprenorphine, diamorphine, methadone, tramadol, pethidine, pentazocine) as first line therapy for mild pain (WHO analgesic ladder not observed; paracetamol or NSAID not prescribed as first-line therapy).

plain_summary: Review a strong opioid started as the first medicine for mild pain. Check which treatments were tried and whether paracetamol or an anti-inflammatory medicine was suitable for this person.

medicine_groups.name: Strong opioids (as named in the criterion)
medicine_groups.note: Count oral and transdermal pain products. Exclude injections and suppositories, including Proladone. Exclude a product identified as treatment for opioid dependence. Biodone Forte oral liquid is a dependence product. If the line says only Biodone and the use is unknown, ask why it was supplied and report at most a possible finding. Targin is oxycodone with naloxone. Diamorphine, pethidine and pentazocine are not normally supplied from a community pharmacy in Australia, so no brand is listed. Codeine, tapentadol and hydromorphone are not named in the criterion and are not in this group. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

medicine_groups.name: First line pain medicines: paracetamol and NSAIDs

paracetamol: Lemsip Cold and Flu Liquid Capsule
Panadol Back and Neck Long Lasting
Panadol Back and Neck Pain Relief
Panadol Children's Drops 1 Month to 2 Years
Tylenol for Babies 1 Month to 2 Years
ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules and liquids count. Skin gels and creams do not count. Products that also hold codeine, such as Panadeine Forte, are not counted here. Paracetamol and some NSAIDs can also be bought without a prescription, which a dispensing history cannot show. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. For these NSAIDs, verify the oral form and that it was used before the opioid for the same pain episode. A brand alone does not establish the form or the episode.

needs_facts.what: Pain severity when the strong opioid was started for this episode
needs_facts.meets: Pain was mild at the start of this opioid for this episode, for example a recorded score of 1 to 3 out of 10.

needs_facts.what: What was the opioid started for?
needs_facts.meets: The supplied opioid was started for this pain episode. Assess pain severity separately.

options.words: To treat this episode of pain
For another reason only, such as dependence treatment or a different pain episode

needs_facts.what: What was tried first for this pain, including paracetamol or an anti-inflammatory bought without a prescription?
needs_facts.meets: The opioid was the first pain medicine for this episode, including medicines from other sources when checking what was tried.

options.words: The opioid was the first pain medicine for this episode
Another pain medicine was tried first for this episode, including any bought without a prescription

rule_for_models: For a person aged 65 or older, flag an oral or transdermal Group A opioid started as the first pain medicine for mild pain and cite the starting supply and the record linking it to that episode. Exclude Biodone Forte, other dependence products, treatment for another indication, moderate or severe pain at the start, and earlier oral paracetamol or an oral NSAID used for the same pain. If the supply otherwise fits but age, the reason for starting the opioid, initial pain severity or treatment order is unclear, report only a possible finding and ask for each missing detail.
cannot_be_seen: Whether paracetamol or an NSAID was tried and bought without a prescription, the cause and real severity of the pain, whether the opioid was started in hospital, and cancer or end of life care.
ask_the_gp: A review of the pain plan, including whether paracetamol or an anti-inflammatory medicine was tried first and whether the strong opioid is still needed.
